articles.title: Most agentic AI projects in production have stalled over data problems
articles.summary: Enterprises are experiencing stalls in agentic AI production deployments primarily due to significant challenges with data quality and governance. Despite increased adoption, these foundational data issues are hindering the transition of AI agents from experimental phases to fully operational production environments.

articles.title: Cyber offenses now account for around a third of all crime across Asia and South Pacific
articles.summary: Interpol reports that cyber-enabled crimes, particularly scams, now constitute approximately one-third of all criminal activity in the Asia-Pacific region. The findings highlight the growing challenge posed by AI-driven threats, especially for regions with limited financial resources for cybersecurity.

articles.title: Leak confirms OpenAI is testing a ChatGPT for Science subscription
articles.summary: Leaked information reveals that OpenAI is in the early stages of developing a specialized ChatGPT subscription tier tailored for scientific research and analysis. It remains uncertain whether this tool will be released to the general public or restricted to specific academic and professional entities.

articles.title: Google to use UK and EU user IP addresses for ad personalization
articles.summary: Google has announced plans to utilize IP addresses from UK, EEA, and Switzerland users for ad personalization and measurement starting in August 2026. This move highlights a shift in policy that faces scrutiny amid ongoing regulatory discussions regarding privacy and consent.

articles.title: Crypto Clipper Campaign Abuses Fake Reviews, AI Narrators, and VirusTotal Comments
articles.summary: An unknown threat actor is deploying a multi-channel campaign to distribute crypto-stealing malware by leveraging fake reviews, AI-generated content, and compromised or fake project pages on platforms like GitHub and SourceForge.

articles.title: Hostile states behind three-quarters of attacks on Britain's critical infrastructure, cyber chief warns
articles.summary: NCSC CEO Richard Horne reports that nation-state actors are responsible for 75% of attacks on UK critical infrastructure and are actively prepositioning for future conflicts. This highlights an increasing risk of sophisticated, state-sponsored cyber-espionage and sabotage.

articles.title: Microsoft Confirms RoguePlanet Defender Zero-Day, Says Patch is in Development
articles.summary: Microsoft is developing a patch for a privilege escalation zero-day vulnerability in the Microsoft Defender Malware Protection Engine, identified as CVE-2026-50656.

articles.title: Massive password-stealing attack hits 75k Fortinet firewalls
articles.summary: Approximately 75,000 Fortinet firewall devices have been targeted in a massive campaign designed to steal administrative credentials. Security experts urge immediate password rotation to mitigate the risk of unauthorized access.

articles.title: FortiBleed Attack Exposes Fortinet Firewall Credentials in 194 Countries
articles.summary: The FortiBleed campaign leveraged compromised credentials to gain unauthorized access to Fortinet firewalls across 194 countries, threatening the security of numerous public and private sector organizations.

articles.title: EU grants Ukraine access to cybersecurity reserve for major attacks
articles.summary: The European Union is granting Ukraine access to its specialized cybersecurity incident response reserve, further integrating the country into the bloc's collective defense framework. This initiative provides Kyiv with professional support to mitigate the impact of large-scale cyberattacks.

articles.title: Junior Hacker Used Tailscale and OpenSSH to Keep Access After His C2 Went Offline
articles.summary: A French-speaking attacker compromised a small automotive business and maintained persistence by installing OpenSSH and Tailscale on victim machines to bypass the reliance on a central command-and-control server.

articles.title: DragonForce Hid Inside Microsoft Teams and Nobody Noticed for Two Months
articles.summary: The DragonForce ransomware group successfully evaded detection for two months by utilizing Microsoft Teams infrastructure to route command-and-control traffic. By leveraging legitimate service relays, the attackers managed to mask malicious activity during an intrusion at a major U.S. services firm.

articles.title: Low-skilled attacker used Claude, Codex to breach 14 companies
articles.summary: OALABS researchers discovered that a low-skilled attacker successfully compromised 14 companies by leveraging AI coding assistants Claude and Codex to bypass safety guardrails. The findings confirm that AI-driven tools are effectively lowering the barrier to entry for conducting sophisticated offensive cyber operations.

articles.title: Attackers hit pair of critical Fortinet vulnerabilities the vendor disclosed in April
articles.summary: Multiple organizations are actively exploiting two critical vulnerabilities in FortiSandbox that were initially disclosed by Fortinet in April. The attacks are coming from various sources, indicating a widespread campaign rather than a single threat actor.

articles.title: U.S. CISA adds Widget Factory Joomla Content Editor flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog
articles.summary: CISA has added the critical CVE-2026-48907 vulnerability affecting Widget Factory's Joomla Content Editor to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog due to evidence of active exploitation.

articles.title: FortiBleed leak exposes Fortinet VPN credentials for 73,000 devices.
articles.summary: The 'FortiBleed' data leak has compromised VPN credentials for nearly 74,000 Fortinet firewall devices globally. This incident poses a significant risk as it provides unauthorized access to enterprise network infrastructure.

articles.title: Digital sovereignty needs an operating model
articles.summary: The article explores the requirement for a structured operating model to achieve digital sovereignty in Europe, focusing on the region's goal to gain greater control over its technological ecosystem. It questions how these high-level political objectives can be translated into practical, sustainable operational frameworks.

articles.title: Another healthcare firm attacked days after Novo Nordisk breach
articles.summary: Medical technology firm iRhythm Holdings suffered a cyberattack leading to the theft of proprietary and patient-protected health information. The incident, disclosed shortly after a breach at Novo Nordisk, involves unauthorized access to third-party-hosted applications and an extortion demand.

articles.title: WitnessAI Agentic Control secures AI agents, tools, and MCP server access
articles.summary: WitnessAI has launched Agentic Control, a security platform designed to provide enterprises with centralized visibility and runtime governance over AI agents, tools, and Model Context Protocol (MCP) server interactions. This solution aims to address security gaps as organizations increasingly deploy AI across development environments and internal workflows.

articles.title: Why Account Takeovers Are Rising and How to Stop Them
articles.summary: Account takeovers are increasing due to advanced tactics like MFA fatigue and session hijacking, prompting a shift toward device trust and continuous verification strategies. This article examines the current threat landscape and provides actionable defense recommendations to mitigate unauthorized access.

articles.title: Tigera introduces unified control plane for Kubernetes-based AI agent security
articles.summary: Tigera has launched Lynx, a unified control plane designed to manage, secure, and monitor AI agents within Kubernetes environments without requiring code modifications. The tool provides identity management, policy enforcement, and anomaly detection to address the unique security challenges posed by AI workloads.

articles.title: Cisco adds another SD-WAN box to max-severity bug advisory
articles.summary: Cisco has updated its security advisory for a maximum-severity vulnerability affecting additional SD-WAN hardware models. Administrators are urged to verify logs for signs of potential compromise even if patches have been applied.

articles.title: Homebrew 6.0 released with new security mechanism, Linux sandbox and more
articles.summary: Homebrew 6.0 has been released, introducing a new security mechanism and Linux sandboxing to improve the package manager's overall security posture. The update follows commentary from the project lead regarding the historical and current vulnerability landscape of package management systems.

articles.title: Rokarolla Android trojan targets banking and crypto users, enables device takeover
articles.summary: The Rokarolla Android banking trojan masquerades as legitimate applications to compromise 217 banking and crypto platforms, granting attackers full device control via accessibility services. Distributed through malicious websites, it poses a significant threat to user financial data and account security.

articles.title: India's Telegram ban hit the UAE too. Here's how to get around it
articles.summary: India's temporary ban on Telegram due to illegal exam paper leaks has caused widespread connectivity disruptions, allegedly exacerbated by BGP hijacking affecting users as far as the UAE. The article outlines the technical cause of the outage and suggests using MTProto proxies to bypass regional restrictions.

articles.title: SpyCloud Report Finds Phishing Attacks Surge as Employee Data Is Exposed at 86% of Fortune 100 Companies
articles.summary: A SpyCloud report reveals that 86% of Fortune 100 companies have suffered exposed employee data, directly contributing to an increase in phishing attacks. This underscores significant vulnerabilities in enterprise identity security.

articles.title: Flip expands platform with digital identity, no-code apps, and AI automation
articles.summary: Flip has introduced 'Frontline Identity' and 'Flip Fusion' to provide secure digital identity, application access, and AI-driven workflow automation specifically for frontline employees. These new tools aim to bridge the gap between mobile communication and enterprise-level system security.

articles.title: Corelight enhances Open NDR to detect AI-driven threats and unknown assets
articles.summary: Corelight has updated its Open NDR platform to improve asset visibility and threat detection, specifically addressing the rapid exploitation risks posed by AI-driven cyber threats. The enhancements integrate passive asset classification with its Zeek-based analysis engine to counter vulnerabilities that outpace traditional patching cycles.

articles.title: 152 Chrome Live Wallpaper Extensions Hid Ad Tracking and Fake Search Clicks
articles.summary: A discovery revealed that 152 Chrome wallpaper extensions were operating as malicious tools, secretly logging user data and generating fraudulent ad clicks. These extensions disguised their traffic to deceive users and ad networks while maintaining a legitimate-looking interface.

articles.title: Heimdal Survey: Executives Four Times More Confident About AI Risk Than the Teams Managing It
articles.summary: A Heimdal survey reveals a significant disconnect, with executives feeling four times more confident in managing AI-related security risks than their operational cybersecurity teams. This disparity highlights a potential misalignment between leadership perception and the practical challenges faced by frontline technical staff.

articles.title: Adversarial Exposure Validation Turns Security Visibility into Confident Prioritization
articles.summary: Security teams are shifting focus from simply detecting risks to validating and prioritizing them to effectively manage overwhelming vulnerability alerts. This approach emphasizes confident decision-making over mere visibility in a complex threat landscape.

articles.title: Microsoft confirms Office apps launch issues after June updates
articles.summary: Microsoft is investigating a technical issue caused by June updates that prevents third-party applications from launching Office programs or opening documents. The problem affects users on fully updated Windows systems.

articles.title: New Rokarolla Android Trojan Targets 217 Banking and Crypto Apps
articles.summary: The newly discovered Rokarolla Android trojan exploits malicious websites to infect devices, enabling attackers to steal financial credentials, intercept communications, and disable security features across 217 banking and crypto applications.

articles.title: ESET MDR vs Sophos MDR: Compared Time to discover and respond to a threat
articles.summary: This article provides a comparative analysis of ESET MDR and Sophos MDR services, focusing on performance metrics like response speed, threat intelligence, and service tiers. It serves as a guide for organizations evaluating managed detection and response solutions.

articles.title: What’s new in Android 17? Anti-theft tools, scam detection, and parental controls
articles.summary: Android 17 has launched with enhanced security features, including new anti-theft tools, real-time scam detection, and improved location privacy controls for users. These updates focus on strengthening OS-level protections and user control over sensitive data.

articles.title: Helpdesk scammers are making house calls to make their lies feel more real
articles.summary: Dutch authorities arrested six individuals, including a teenager, linked to a fraudulent call center that escalates cyber-enabled bank scams by conducting in-person 'house calls' to victims. This tactic highlights a concerning evolution in social engineering where physical presence is used to increase the perceived legitimacy of scams.

articles.title: The Top 10 Attack Surface Exposures in 2026
articles.summary: The article highlights how internet-facing attack surface exposures, ranging from exposed admin panels to zero-day vulnerabilities like MongoBleed, significantly increase the risk of rapid exploitation. It emphasizes that attackers are increasingly reducing the time between vulnerability disclosure and successful exploitation.

articles.title: Warner warns of CISA cuts, staffing gaps in letter to acting chief
articles.summary: Senator Mark Warner has urged the DHS to address funding shortages and staffing gaps at CISA, specifically highlighting the need to secure financial support for the Multi-State Information Sharing and Analysis Center (MS-ISAC).

articles.title: CISA orders feds to patch max severity Joomla plugin flaw by Friday
articles.summary: CISA has issued an emergency directive requiring federal agencies to remediate a critical, actively exploited vulnerability in the Widget Factory Joomla Content Editor (JCE) plugin by the end of the week. This order aims to prevent potential compromises stemming from the ongoing exploitation of the maximum-severity security flaw.

articles.title: The Chainguard Athena coalition already shipped 2,000 patches across 500 open source projects
articles.summary: Chainguard has launched the Athena coalition, an industry group that identifies and patches vulnerabilities in open source projects under embargo before public disclosure. The initiative has already remediated 2,000 vulnerabilities across 500 projects with the support of major member organizations.

articles.title: Malicious JetBrains Plugins Steal AI API Keys as Chrome Extensions Capture Chatbot Chats
articles.summary: A coordinated malware campaign has compromised the JetBrains Marketplace, deploying 15 malicious plugins designed to steal AI API keys and capture sensitive chatbot data. These plugins masquerade as legitimate AI coding assistants to deceive developers into compromising their development environments.

articles.title: EdTech Faces a Cybersecurity Crisis: Data Breaches Surge
articles.summary: The EdTech sector is facing an increasing frequency of cyberattacks from threat actors like ShinyHunters and FulcrumSec, leading to significant data breaches and service disruptions. Resecurity warns that educational institutions and their platforms are currently prime targets for malicious cyber activity.

articles.title: Ukraine can now tap EU cyber support during major attacks
articles.summary: Ukraine has been added to the EU Cybersecurity Reserve, allowing the country to access emergency incident response services from trusted private-sector providers during major cyberattacks. This integration enhances Ukraine's resilience by leveraging the resources of the European Union Agency for Cybersecurity (ENISA).

articles.title: FulcrumSec Targets Novo Nordisk, Leaks Clinical and Research Data
articles.summary: The extortion group FulcrumSec leaked 1.3TB of stolen data, including clinical and AI research records, from Novo Nordisk after the company refused a $25 million ransom demand.

articles.title: Microsoft working on Defender patch for RoguePlanet zero-day
articles.summary: Microsoft is actively developing a security patch to address the RoguePlanet zero-day vulnerability affecting its Defender software. The flaw was disclosed one week ago, prompting an official response from the company.

articles.title: Apple is bringing Hide My Email and Sign in with Apple under one domain
articles.summary: Apple is consolidating the email domains for its 'Sign in with Apple' and 'Hide My Email' services under a single domain, private.icloud.com, starting this summer. This update aims to unify infrastructure for these privacy-focused email forwarding features.

articles.title: 15 Malicious JetBrains Plugins Caught Stealing DeepSeek, OpenAI API Keys
articles.summary: Threat actors have uploaded 15 malicious JetBrains plugins disguised as AI coding assistants to exfiltrate sensitive API keys, including those for OpenAI and DeepSeek. This campaign specifically targets software developers to compromise their development environments.

articles.title: China-Linked FishMonger Ports SprySOCKS to Windows With Kernel-Level Stealth and UEFI Bootkit Hints
articles.summary: China-linked threat actor FishMonger has expanded its arsenal by deploying new Windows-based variants of the SprySOCKS backdoor, which utilize kernel-level drivers and print spooler vulnerabilities to target government entities. Previously known only as a Linux threat, this malware now incorporates advanced persistence mechanisms including potential UEFI bootkit integration.

articles.title: 144 Mastra npm Packages Compromised via Hijacked Contributor Account
articles.summary: 144 Mastra npm packages were compromised after a contributor's account was hijacked to distribute malicious code through a supply chain attack dubbed easy-day-js. Security researchers confirmed the incident, highlighting a significant vulnerability within the AI framework's ecosystem.

articles.title: Fortinet FortiSOC unifies SIEM, SOAR, threat intelligence, and AI in one platform
articles.summary: Fortinet has launched FortiSOC, a unified SaaS platform that integrates SIEM, SOAR, threat intelligence, and agentic AI to streamline security operations and autonomous incident response. The platform aims to simplify SecOps management by consolidating multiple functions into a single, cloud-delivered console.

articles.title: Kodak confirms data breach claimed by ShinyHunters extortion gang
articles.summary: Kodak is investigating a data breach after the ShinyHunters extortion gang claimed to have compromised some of the company's internal data.

articles.title: The SOC’s visibility gap comes down to staffing
articles.summary: While AI adoption in security operations centers is widespread, a significant portion of teams lack the structured governance and standardized workflows necessary to effectively utilize these tools. This inconsistent implementation creates a visibility gap that stems from inadequate staffing and strategic planning.

articles.title: CISA Warns of Actively Exploited Joomla JCE Flaw Allowing PHP Code Execution
articles.summary: CISA has added a critical-severity vulnerability in the Joomla Content Editor (JCE) to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog due to confirmed active exploitation. The flaw allows for arbitrary PHP code execution through improper access control.

articles.title: Microsoft AntiSSRF open-source library helps block server-side request forgery
articles.summary: Microsoft has released an open-source library called AntiSSRF to help developers mitigate server-side request forgery vulnerabilities by validating URLs and network connections in .NET and Node.js applications.

articles.title: Navigating SEC, NIS2, and DORA incident disclosure timelines under pressure
articles.summary: This video discusses the operational challenges of managing overlapping incident disclosure requirements under SEC, NIS2, and DORA regulations during a potential data breach. It highlights the complexities global organizations face when navigating differing regulatory reporting timelines.

articles.title: The checklist problem behind critical infrastructure cyber safety
articles.summary: New research from George Mason University highlights that meeting federal cybersecurity compliance standards does not guarantee protection against physical system failures or cyberattacks in critical infrastructure. The study argues that current policies treat compliance as a proxy for safety, leaving operational technology vulnerable despite meeting regulatory checklists.

articles.title: Cyberattack sees crops kept in the ground
articles.summary: Australian sugar producer Mackay Sugar experienced a cyberattack during its peak cane crushing season, resulting in operational delays that forced crops to remain unharvested. The incident highlights the significant impact of digital disruptions on critical agricultural supply chains.

articles.title: India's Telegram ban draws criticism from Durov as company challenges order in court
articles.summary: Indian authorities have ordered a nationwide restriction on Telegram to prevent exam malpractice, prompting a legal challenge and public criticism from the platform's founder, Pavel Durov.

articles.title: GitHub dismissed security reports on flaws now exploited by supply-chain worm, researchers say
articles.summary: GitHub reportedly dismissed vulnerability reports regarding design flaws that are now being exploited by the Shai-Hulud supply-chain worm to compromise numerous software packages. These security gaps have led to widespread infections across developer accounts and repositories.

articles.title: Malicious JetBrains Marketplace plugins steal AI API keys from developers
articles.summary: At least 15 malicious plugins identified on the JetBrains Marketplace have been found exfiltrating sensitive AI API keys from developer environments. This supply chain compromise poses a significant risk to the security of developer credentials and integrated AI services.

articles.title: Lawmakers leary about Trump administration’s Anthropic order
articles.summary: Members of Congress have expressed skepticism and requested further clarification regarding the Trump administration's directive involving AI company Anthropic. Responses from lawmakers emphasize a cautious approach to the executive action.

articles.title: AI’s constant patching treadmill can be a security problem
articles.summary: Rapid release cycles for AI models are forcing developers to choose between performance and security, potentially creating silent vulnerabilities. This creates an ongoing maintenance burden that may compromise overall system integrity.

articles.title: Python dev saved from disaster by intuition... and AI
articles.summary: A Python developer avoided a potentially catastrophic system compromise after an AI-powered tool identified and blocked a malicious repository. The incident highlights the growing role of AI in detecting automated supply chain attacks.

articles.title: Python dev saved from disaster by intuition...and AI
articles.summary: A developer avoided a potentially destructive repository installation after an AI tool intervened and warned of the risks. This highlights the growing role of AI in identifying and preventing malicious code execution during the development lifecycle.

articles.title: New Rokarolla Android malware targets 217 banking, crypto apps
articles.summary: The newly discovered Rokarolla Android banking trojan is actively targeting 217 financial and cryptocurrency applications through a robust suite of 137 distinct commands. This malware poses a significant threat to mobile users by attempting to compromise sensitive banking and digital asset credentials.

articles.title: iRhythm Hit by Cyberattack, Patient Data Stolen and Ransom Demanded
articles.summary: Digital healthcare provider iRhythm suffered a data breach involving the theft of patient and proprietary information via third-party apps, resulting in a ransom demand. The incident impacts sensitive cardiac monitoring data collected through the company's Zio wearable technology.

articles.title: Google Vertex AI SDK Flaw Let Attackers Hijack Model Uploads via Bucket Squatting
articles.summary: A vulnerability in the Google Cloud Vertex AI SDK for Python allowed unauthorized attackers to hijack model uploads and execute arbitrary code via a bucket squatting technique dubbed 'Pickle in the Middle'.

articles.title: Steam Workshop abused to spread malware via Wallpaper Engine app
articles.summary: Threat actors are exploiting Valve's Steam Workshop to distribute malicious software disguised as wallpaper packages for the Wallpaper Engine app. This campaign leverages the platform's trusted ecosystem to infect unsuspecting users through community-shared content.

articles.title: Three critical Fortinet sandbox bugs splattered by unknown attackers
articles.summary: Unknown attackers are exploiting three critical vulnerabilities in Fortinet's sandbox technology. Users are strongly advised to update to the latest patched versions to mitigate the risk.

articles.title: ClickFix Campaigns Expand Malware Delivery With New Loaders and Fake Update Lures
articles.summary: Multiple ClickFix campaigns are actively distributing three new malware loaders—BabaDeda, Lorem Ipsum, and Potemkin—targeting sectors including education and finance. These attacks utilize deceptive fake update lures to compromise systems.

articles.title: Amos Stealer Targets macOS Keychain Files and Browser Passwords
articles.summary: Amos Stealer is a malicious campaign targeting macOS users that utilizes deceptive downloads to exfiltrate sensitive data, including Keychain files, browser credentials, and developer configuration files. It represents a significant threat to user privacy and system security by harvesting high-value authentication information.

articles.title: A case for how to shape ‘ingredient lists’ for AI models
articles.summary: Policymakers are exploring the implementation of AI bills of materials (AIBOMs) to establish a standardized framework for transparency and regulation in AI models. This roadmap aims to help stakeholders identify key components and security implications within AI development.

articles.title: India temporarily blocks Telegram over medical exam cheating fears
articles.summary: Indian authorities have temporarily blocked Telegram to prevent the misuse of the platform by scammers facilitating exam cheating through misleading information. The measure addresses concerns that bad actors were manipulating content to simulate exam leaks.

articles.title: Attackers are exploiting FortiSandbox vulnerabilities
articles.summary: Attackers are actively exploiting three vulnerabilities in FortiSandbox, a critical component for threat enforcement within Fortinet ecosystems. Threat intelligence reports suggest the exploits currently in circulation may be unstable or faulty.

articles.title: Aembit Extends IAM for Agentic AI to Microsoft Copilot Studio
articles.summary: Aembit has expanded its Identity and Access Management (IAM) capabilities to support Microsoft Copilot Studio, enhancing security for AI agents. This integration aims to help organizations manage and secure identities used by agentic AI workflows.

articles.title: Crooks found a new way to collaborate using Teams – by hiding command-and-control traffic
articles.summary: Threat actors are leveraging Microsoft Teams as a command-and-control channel for custom malware, allowing malicious traffic to blend in with legitimate corporate communications. This technique makes detection significantly harder by masquerading attack activity as routine collaboration.

articles.title: UK to require ID or face scan before you can make social media accounts
articles.summary: The UK government will mandate age verification via ID or facial scans for new social media accounts starting in 2027 to restrict access for those under 16. Security experts have raised concerns that these measures may be easily bypassed and introduce significant data privacy and security risks.

articles.title: Cybercriminals mask malicious communications through Microsoft Teams relays
articles.summary: The DragonForce ransomware group is exploiting Microsoft Teams TURN infrastructure to obfuscate command-and-control traffic using custom 'Backdoor.Turn' malware. This technique allows attackers to mask malicious communications within legitimate enterprise collaboration traffic.

articles.title: Fortinet Warned as Three Critical FortiSandbox Bugs Come Under Attack
articles.summary: Three critical vulnerabilities in Fortinet FortiSandbox are being actively exploited in the wild, including two flaws that remained unpatched for months and one recently disclosed bug. This situation highlights the urgent need for organizations to prioritize security updates to close the window of vulnerability.

articles.title: GhostTree Attack Abused Recursive Windows Junctions to Hide Malware
articles.summary: The GhostTree attack leverages recursive NTFS junctions to create an infinite file path structure, effectively trapping Microsoft Defender in a scanning loop to hide malicious files. This technique allows malware to bypass detection by causing security software to hang indefinitely during folder scans.

articles.title: TekStream launches Proactive Cyber Defense to counter AI-driven threats
articles.summary: TekStream has introduced a new Proactive Cyber Defense service powered by their Cosmos platform to help organizations mitigate risks from AI-accelerated and autonomous cyber threats. The service aims to address the challenges of machine-speed attacks and increasing operational complexity in modern security environments.

articles.title: FTC warns of record $3.5 billion losses to imposter scams in 2025
articles.summary: The U.S. FTC reported that Americans suffered record losses of $3.5 billion to imposter scams in 2025, marking a nearly threefold increase in financial damage since 2020.

articles.title: SimpleHelp RMM flaw could give attackers full access to managed endpoints (CVE-2026-48558)
articles.summary: A critical authentication bypass vulnerability (CVE-2026-48558) in SimpleHelp RMM allows unauthenticated attackers to create unauthorized technician accounts and gain full remote control over managed endpoints. This flaw impacts deployments using OpenID Connect and persists even when MFA is enabled.

articles.title: New Rokarolla Android Malware Steals PINs, SMS Codes, and Crypto Wallet Funds
articles.summary: Rokarolla is a sophisticated Android banking trojan that grants attackers extensive control over infected devices, enabling the theft of credentials, SMS codes, and cryptocurrency assets. It actively targets hundreds of financial applications while maintaining persistent access by disabling security features like Google Play Protect.

articles.title: AppViewX extends machine identity security to AI agents and post-quantum environments
articles.summary: AppViewX has launched a new Agent Identity Security solution designed to manage and secure AI agents and prepare enterprise environments for post-quantum cryptographic challenges. The platform provides a centralized control plane for governing machine and agent identities to mitigate risks from emerging technologies.

articles.title: AppViewX Launches Agent Identity Security to Govern Agents for the AI and Quantum Era
articles.summary: AppViewX has introduced Agent Identity Security, a new solution designed to manage and govern AI agents and machine identities to prepare for the evolving security challenges of the AI and quantum computing era.

articles.title: New Rokarolla Android Trojan Found Targeting 217 Crypto and Banking Apps
articles.summary: Zimperium researchers have identified a new Android Trojan named Rokarolla that hijacks clipboards, intercepts banking calls, and gains full device control to target 217 financial and cryptocurrency applications. The malware poses a significant threat to mobile banking security by enabling comprehensive unauthorized access.

articles.title: Teleport adds LLM Proxy and Delegated Identity to secure AI agent actions and access
articles.summary: Teleport has introduced LLM Proxy and Delegated Identity features in its Beams beta to enhance security, access control, and auditability for AI agent workflows. These tools aim to bridge critical gaps in managing what AI agents are permitted to access and how they execute tasks.

articles.title: Radware AI Xploit Shield delivers virtual patching for newly identified application and API flaws
articles.summary: Radware has introduced AI Xploit Shield, a service designed to provide virtual patching for applications and APIs to counter the rapid exploitation of newly discovered vulnerabilities accelerated by AI models. It aims to bridge the security gap between vulnerability identification and traditional remediation timelines.

articles.title: Developer laptops are the credential store attackers are picking through in 2026, GitGuardian announces Endpoint Protection
articles.summary: GitGuardian has launched an Endpoint Protection solution designed to secure developer laptops, which have become a primary target for attackers seeking sensitive credentials. This development addresses the rising trend of threat actors exploiting unsecured developer workstations to gain unauthorized access to production environments.

articles.title: Cardiac monitor maker's security skips a beat as data thieves go for the jugular
articles.summary: Attackers gained unauthorized access to patient data by leveraging social engineering tactics to compromise third-party business applications used by a cardiac monitor manufacturer.

articles.title: Survey: 94% of Incidents Involve Anonymized Infrastructure. Teams Are Still Reactive
articles.summary: Despite an abundance of threat intelligence data, 94% of security incidents involve anonymized infrastructure, highlighting that organizations remain largely reactive due to the difficulty of attributing such activity. Security teams struggle to effectively distill vast amounts of IP data into actionable insights to identify threat actors.

articles.title: CVE-2026-20262: CISCO Catalyst SD-WAN Flaw Under Active Targeted Exploitation
articles.summary: Cisco has confirmed that CVE-2026-20262, an arbitrary file write vulnerability in its Catalyst SD-WAN Manager, is currently being exploited in the wild.

articles.title: Best of Android Fax Apps: Top 5 Secure Picks for 2026
articles.summary: This article provides a curated list of the top five secure Android fax applications available for 2026, comparing various tools for document transmission. It serves as a guide for users seeking secure mobile document exchange solutions.

articles.title: CISA warns of another cPanel plugin flaw exploited in attacks
articles.summary: CISA has issued an emergency directive requiring federal agencies to secure their servers against an actively exploited vulnerability in the LiteSpeed cPanel plugin within three days.

articles.title: Attackers Exploit Three Fortinet FortiSandbox Flaws, One Patched Last Week
articles.summary: Threat intelligence firm Defused Cyber reports that attackers are actively exploiting three vulnerabilities in Fortinet FortiSandbox, including one that was recently patched.

articles.title: Cisco discloses second exploited SD-WAN vulnerability in two weeks (CVE-2026-20262)
articles.summary: Cisco has disclosed a critical, actively exploited vulnerability (CVE-2026-20262) affecting its Catalyst SD-WAN Manager, marking the second such exploit reported within two weeks. The situation is notable as Cisco claims the flaw was identified through internal testing, yet evidence indicates attackers were already leveraging it prior to public disclosure.

articles.title: Ransomware gang abuses Microsoft Teams relays to hide malicious traffic
articles.summary: The DragonForce ransomware group is utilizing a custom backdoor to mask malicious command-and-control traffic by routing it through Microsoft Teams relay infrastructure. This technique allows attackers to bypass security monitoring by blending in with legitimate corporate communications.

articles.title: Crypto scammers are sending couriers to victims’ homes to collect cash
articles.summary: The FBI has issued a warning regarding a rise in cryptocurrency investment scams where perpetrators dispatch physical couriers to collect cash from victims. This tactic is used to bypass financial institution monitoring and security blocks on fraudulent transfers.

articles.title: Pickle in the Middle – Hijacking Vertex AI Model Uploads for Cross-Tenant RCE
articles.summary: Unit 42 identified a vulnerability in the Vertex AI Python SDK that enables remote code execution through bucket squatting. This flaw allows attackers to compromise cross-tenant model uploads.

articles.title: China-Linked SprySOCKS Backdoor Expands to Windows with Driver-Based Stealth
articles.summary: Cybersecurity researchers have identified two new Windows-based variants of the previously Linux-exclusive SprySOCKS backdoor, which utilize driver-based techniques to enhance stealth. These variants feature hard-coded command-and-control configurations and support multiple communication protocols.

articles.title: Software supply chains are heading for a transparency test
articles.summary: The upcoming EU Cyber Resilience Act is compelling organizations to adopt Software Bill of Materials (SBOM) practices to ensure supply chain transparency and regulatory compliance by 2027. This transition shifts SBOM management from an optional best practice to a mandatory requirement for software manufacturers.

articles.title: Critical Fortinet FortiSandbox flaws now exploited in attacks
articles.summary: Critical vulnerabilities in Fortinet's FortiSandbox platform are currently being exploited by attackers in the wild. Security researchers warn that these flaws require immediate patching to prevent potential compromise.

articles.title: Windows version of SprySOCKS Linux malware used to attack govt orgs
articles.summary: A Windows version of the SprySOCKS Linux malware has been identified in targeted cyberattacks against government organizations across four countries. This discovery highlights the evolution of the threat actor's toolkit to expand their reach across different operating systems.

articles.title: U.S. CISA adds Cisco Catalyst and LiteSpeed cPanel plugin flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog
articles.summary: CISA has added two critical vulnerabilities in Cisco Catalyst and the LiteSpeed cPanel plugin to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog due to evidence of active exploitation.

articles.title: Planning a trip? Fake travel sites are multiplying this summer
articles.summary: Cyberattacks against the travel and hospitality sector have surged by 122% over three years, with a notable spike in malicious travel-related domain registrations. This trend highlights a significant increase in consumer-facing phishing and fraudulent site activities ahead of peak travel seasons.

articles.title: Fake Microsoft Alerts Used to Deploy North Korean NarwhalRAT Malware
articles.summary: The North Korean hacking group APT37 is utilizing spear-phishing emails that impersonate Microsoft security alerts to deploy the NarwhalRAT malware. The campaign targets users by leveraging fake account security concerns to gain unauthorized access.

articles.title: China-linked actor spent two years inside medical research networks
articles.summary: A China-linked threat actor known as UNC6508 maintained undetected access to North American medical and military research networks for two years to exfiltrate sensitive data. The group utilized stealthy techniques, including credential theft and email forwarding, to sustain their long-term espionage campaign.

articles.title: GitHub releases an open dataset for multilingual developer content
articles.summary: GitHub has released an open dataset of multilingual developer content, including README files and discussions, to facilitate research into non-English public repositories. This initiative aligns with Microsoft’s European Digital Commitments to foster more inclusive software development environments.

articles.title: iRhythm discloses data breach, says hackers stole patient info
articles.summary: Digital healthcare provider iRhythm Holdings reported a data breach involving the unauthorized access and theft of patient personal and health information from third-party business applications.

articles.title: Cisco Releases Security Updates for Actively Exploited SD-WAN Manager Flaw
articles.summary: Cisco has issued security patches for a medium-severity vulnerability in its Catalyst SD-WAN Manager, which is currently being exploited by attackers in the wild.

articles.title: Reachability makes AI threat modeling worth the trust
articles.summary: Oscar Andersson of Oplane argues that traditional security scanning tools produce excessive false positives and emphasizes the importance of reachability analysis in validating threats within real-world code. By focusing only on paths that lead to an actual impact, security teams can better prioritize genuine vulnerabilities.

articles.title: CISA Flags LiteSpeed cPanel Plugin Flaw Exploited for Root Privilege Escalation
articles.summary: CISA has added the CVE-2026-54420 vulnerability in the LiteSpeed cPanel Plugin to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog due to active exploitation for root privilege escalation. Federal agencies are mandated to remediate the flaw by June 18, 2026.

articles.title: EU Cybersecurity Act 2.0: When good regulation goes bad
articles.summary: The article critiques the proposed EU Cybersecurity Act 2.0, arguing that while the intention to improve infrastructure security is positive, the actual policy framework may be flawed or ineffective.

articles.title: A $2 trillion revenue shift hinges on AI data governance
articles.summary: Large enterprises are struggling to scale AI initiatives due to fragmented data governance and difficulty in verifying customer data consent. This lack of automated compliance is causing significant delays and hindering potential revenue growth.

articles.title: Cybersecurity jobs available right now: June 16, 2026
articles.summary: Help Net Security provides a curated list of cybersecurity job openings for June 16, 2026, highlighting specific roles such as Android Vulnerability Researcher and Application Security Engineer.

articles.title: UK to ban social media access for children under 16
articles.summary: The UK government is planning to implement a ban preventing children under 16 from accessing social media platforms that feature user interaction and algorithms. This policy aims to increase online safety for minors by restricting their exposure to certain digital environments.

articles.title: Inside the Modern SOC: The 72-Minute Race
articles.summary: Modern security operations centers must accelerate response times to counter attackers who can complete exfiltration in just 72 minutes, leveraging AI-driven automation and MDR. This highlights the critical need for speed in threat detection and mitigation.

articles.title: Estonia to quarantine emails sent from Russian .ru domain before they reach government officials
articles.summary: The Estonian government is implementing mandatory security screenings for all incoming emails from Russian .ru domains to protect officials from potential cyber threats. This measure acts as a precautionary defensive layer against state-sponsored digital risks.

articles.title: DOJ seizes CFAKE, SOCFAKE deepfake nude sites under TAKE IT DOWN Act
articles.summary: The U.S. Department of Justice seized two websites, CFAKE.com and SOCFAKE.com, for hosting nonconsensual AI-generated explicit content, marking the first enforcement action under the TAKE IT DOWN Act.

articles.title: Cisco SD-WAN make-me-root bug under attack
articles.summary: Cisco's Catalyst SD-WAN Manager is facing active exploitation of a 'make-me-root' vulnerability, marking the second zero-day flaw targeting the platform this month.

articles.title: Feds freaked over Fable 5 after simple 'fix this code' prompt, not jailbreak, says researcher
articles.summary: A researcher claims federal authorities overreacted to a report involving Fable 5, noting that the incident stemmed from a simple code correction prompt rather than a malicious jailbreak attempt.

articles.title: Google exposes China espionage group that’s been lurking in networks undetected since 2023
articles.summary: Google has uncovered a Chinese state-sponsored espionage group that has been covertly operating within critical infrastructure networks since 2023. The actors utilized backdoors to facilitate data theft and intelligence gathering.

articles.title: SimpleHelp bug lets hackers create rogue remote support accounts
articles.summary: A vulnerability in SimpleHelp remote management software permits unauthenticated attackers to create unauthorized, privileged technician accounts by exploiting the OpenID Connect protocol. This flaw exposes servers to full remote control by malicious actors.

articles.title: Chinese Hackers Abused Google Workspace Rules to Steal Research and Defense Emails
articles.summary: A China-linked espionage group compromised North American research and military networks by exploiting REDCap server vulnerabilities to steal credentials. The attackers subsequently manipulated Google Workspace forwarding rules to covertly exfiltrate sensitive research and defense emails.

articles.title: North Korean Hackers Are Turning Developer Tools Into Malware Delivery Channels
articles.summary: North Korean threat actors known as Contagious Interview are leveraging developer-focused phishing campaigns to distribute malware. The attacks utilize recruitment and code review themes to compromise software development environments.

articles.title: Australian Sugar Producer Mackay Sugar Reports Cyber Incident
articles.summary: Mackay Sugar, Australia's second-largest sugar manufacturer, has reported a cyberattack that may have disrupted its primary processing operations. The company is currently investigating the incident to determine the extent of the impact on its systems.

articles.title: Chinese hackers breached North American research institutions via REDCap servers
articles.summary: The China-linked threat actor UNC6508 compromised North American medical research institutions by exploiting vulnerabilities in REDCap servers to deploy custom malware. The group maintained persistent, undetected access for over a year to exfiltrate sensitive information.

articles.title: Maine closes data breach portal to the public after fake reports
articles.summary: The Maine Attorney General's office has restricted public access to its data breach reporting portal following a series of fraudulent breach submissions. The portal will remain closed for public viewing while the state conducts an audit to implement stronger security controls.

articles.title: Council of Europe hacked in ShinyHunters' PeopleSoft heist
articles.summary: The Council of Europe has been compromised in a PeopleSoft data heist conducted by the threat actor group ShinyHunters. This incident is part of a larger campaign affecting over 100 other organizations, including Nottingham University.

articles.title: OptinMonster WordPress plugin hacked in CDN supply-chain attack
articles.summary: The OptinMonster, TrustPulse, and PushEngage WordPress plugins were compromised through a supply-chain attack involving the Awesome Motive content distribution network. The incident allowed unauthorized code injection, potentially affecting users of these widely installed plugins.

articles.title: Cisco fixes SD-WAN vManage flaw exploited in zero-day attacks
articles.summary: Cisco has released security patches to address a critical vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-20262, in its Catalyst SD-WAN Manager that was actively exploited by attackers to achieve root privilege escalation.

articles.title: Feds snooze as US datacenter law set to lapse with no replacement in site
articles.summary: The Federal Data Center Enhancement Act of 2023, which mandates security and sustainability standards, is set to expire without a replacement in place. This legislative lapse risks leaving federal data centers without updated regulatory oversight for critical infrastructure protection.

articles.title: LiteLLM Vulnerability Chain Lets Low-Privilege Users Take Over AI Gateway Servers
articles.summary: A chain of three vulnerabilities in the LiteLLM proxy allows low-privilege users to escalate privileges to administrator status and execute arbitrary code on AI gateway servers. This exploit poses a significant risk as it grants unauthorized access to all API keys and secrets managed by the proxy.

articles.title: Council of Europe investigates ShinyHunters data breach claims
articles.summary: The Council of Europe is investigating claims made by the threat actor group ShinyHunters regarding a potential data breach. The intergovernmental organization is currently working to verify the legitimacy of these extortion-related allegations.

articles.title: Cybersecurity experts don’t think Anthropic’s Fable 5 presents a unique threat
articles.summary: Cybersecurity experts argue that Anthropic's Fable 5 model does not offer unique hacking capabilities, viewing recent export controls on the technology as misguided.

articles.title: Microsoft site throwing warnings after someone forgot to renew cert
articles.summary: Microsoft's connectivity checker service triggered browser security warnings due to an expired SSL certificate. The issue was caused by an administrative oversight regarding the renewal of security credentials.

articles.title: FBI: Fraudsters use couriers to steal money in crypto scams
articles.summary: The FBI has issued a warning regarding a rise in cryptocurrency scams where fraudsters dispatch physical couriers to collect cash directly from victims. These schemes are frequently associated with pig butchering and romance baiting tactics.

articles.title: China-linked spies backdoored authentication stack to stay hidden for years
articles.summary: A China-linked threat actor known as Velvet Ant maintained long-term, stealthy access to an unnamed organization's network by compromising the entire authentication stack. The group remained undetected for nearly a decade, highlighting their sophisticated persistence capabilities.

articles.title: One-Click Microsoft 365 Copilot Flaw Could Have Let Attackers Steal Emails, Files, and MFA Codes
articles.summary: Researchers discovered a 'SearchLeak' vulnerability in Microsoft 365 Copilot that allows attackers to exfiltrate sensitive data via a single, trusted link. By chaining three bugs, attackers could bypass security filters to steal emails, files, and multi-factor authentication codes.

articles.title: Cyberattack on Russian tech firm Astral disrupts business, government services for week
articles.summary: A cyberattack on the Russian technology firm Astral caused week-long service outages, significantly impacting business operations, regulatory compliance systems, and government-linked services. The disruption hindered essential functions such as digital document management, point-of-sale systems, and authentication protocols.

articles.title: Delinea and Cyera integrate for data-aware identity security
articles.summary: Delinea and Cyera have integrated their platforms to correlate privileged identity access with sensitive data exposure, enabling better risk prioritization for human and machine identities. This partnership aims to help security teams govern access paths in environments increasingly populated by AI agents.

articles.title: Vibe coders are gonna vibe code: How CISOs are tackling code sprawl
articles.summary: The rise of AI-driven 'vibe coding' by employees is creating significant shadow IT and governance challenges for CISOs. Organizations are struggling to maintain security oversight as staff deploy automated tools and applications outside traditional corporate controls.

articles.title: PRC-linked spies hid inside medical and military networks for more than a year, snooping through Gmail and stealing data
articles.summary: PRC-linked threat actors maintained persistent unauthorized access to medical and military networks for over a year, exfiltrating sensitive data and monitoring Gmail communications. The attackers specifically targeted intellectual property related to drone technology and biological research.

articles.title: Chinese hackers breach REDCap servers, steal medical research
articles.summary: Chinese-linked threat actors compromised vulnerable REDCap servers at a North American medical institution to deploy InfiniteRed malware and exfiltrate sensitive research data.

articles.title: ⚡ Weekly Recap: Chrome 0-Day, UniFi Exploits, macOS Stealers, VPN Flaw and More
articles.summary: The weekly recap highlights recurring cybersecurity threats, including critical Chrome zero-days, exposed legacy infrastructure, and the exploitation of abandoned software components. It emphasizes that persistent vulnerabilities and negligence remain the primary entry points for modern cyber attacks.

articles.title: Feds Seize CFAKE and SOCFAKE Over Explicit Deepfakes of Famous Women
articles.summary: U.S. federal authorities seized the domains CFAKE.com and SOCFAKE.com for hosting nonconsensual, AI-generated deepfake explicit imagery of famous women. This action highlights ongoing legal efforts to combat the proliferation of synthetic sexual abuse material.

articles.title: Arch Linux locks down AUR signups amid wave of malicious commits
articles.summary: Arch Linux has temporarily suspended new account registrations on the Arch User Repository (AUR) to counter a surge of malicious software contributions. The move aims to prevent the distribution of poisoned packages within the community-driven platform.

articles.title: Finland brings charges against cargo ship officers for cutting submarine cables
articles.summary: Finnish prosecutors have charged cargo ship officers with damaging subsea telecommunications cables and attempting to compromise additional connections. The incident highlights the growing concern over the physical security of critical digital infrastructure.

articles.title: 1Password Credential Broker reduces secret sprawl through identity-based credential delivery
articles.summary: 1Password has introduced the 1Password Credential Broker, a new solution designed to mitigate secret sprawl by providing secure, identity-based delivery of credentials and tokens to machine workloads and humans. The tool is currently in private beta and aims to centralize access management for systems like GitHub Actions.

articles.title: Novo Nordisk Confirms Data Theft: What Attackers Took and What They Didn’t
articles.summary: Novo Nordisk confirmed a data breach involving unauthorized access to internal systems and the theft of personal clinical trial data. The company is currently investigating the incident, for which no threat actor has yet claimed responsibility.

articles.title: Trust3 AI’s AgentDOS monitors AI agent activity, data access, and token consumption
articles.summary: Trust3 AI has launched AgentDOS, an enterprise control plane designed to monitor AI agent behavior, data access, and token usage to mitigate risks associated with autonomous AI deployment. The platform addresses emerging concerns regarding security compliance and unauthorized agent activity in corporate environments.

articles.title: New attack turned Microsoft 365 Copilot into 1-click data theft tool
articles.summary: A critical vulnerability chain called SearchLeak allows attackers to exploit Microsoft 365 Copilot via malicious URLs to exfiltrate sensitive data from OneDrive, SharePoint, and mailbox accounts. The flaw essentially turns the AI assistant into a mechanism for one-click data theft.

articles.title: Omada Agent Governance helps organizations manage AI agent access, risk, and compliance
articles.summary: Omada has introduced a new governance solution aimed at managing the security, access, and compliance risks associated with autonomous AI agents and non-human identities within enterprise environments.

articles.title: Ukrainian national pleads guilty in connection with Conti ransomware
articles.summary: A Ukrainian national, Oleksii Oleksiyovych Lytvynenko, has pleaded guilty to conspiracy to commit wire fraud for his role in the Conti ransomware operation that impacted over 1,000 victims globally. Lytvynenko admitted to joining the criminal conspiracy in 2021 and possessing data stolen from multiple U.S. and international victims.

articles.title: Anthropic says US government forced it to disable cybersecurity AI models
articles.summary: The US government invoked national security authorities to mandate that Anthropic disable specific cybersecurity AI models, marking a significant precedent in AI export control. This action suggests a shift in regulatory focus from hardware restrictions to the direct limitation of advanced software capabilities.

articles.title: Red Sift, GMO GlobalSign partnership simplifies email authentication and BIMI adoption
articles.summary: Red Sift and GMO GlobalSign have partnered to streamline the process of implementing email authentication and BIMI adoption for organizations. This integration allows users to manage secure outbound email protection and obtain Verified Mark Certificates through a single platform.

articles.title: Webinar: How behavioral AI stops phishing and account takeovers
articles.summary: This webinar discusses how behavioral AI technology can enhance email security by automating the detection and remediation of phishing and account takeover attacks to alleviate operational strain. It focuses on modernizing defense strategies against sophisticated threats that circumvent traditional security controls.

articles.title: Handala Hacking Group Claims Breach of California Water Service
articles.summary: The Handala hacking group claims to have breached California Water Service, resulting in the exposure of 5GB of customer data and infrastructure files. This incident highlights an ongoing threat to critical infrastructure sectors.

articles.title: AI vulnerability discovery is pushing 2026 CVEs toward 66,000
articles.summary: The rapid adoption of AI-driven vulnerability discovery tools is significantly accelerating the identification of software flaws, leading to a projected record of 66,000 CVEs for 2026. This surge in automated reporting suggests a fundamental shift in how security vulnerabilities are uncovered at scale.

articles.title: The Onboarding Password Mistake That Creates Unnecessary Risk
articles.summary: The common IT practice of providing new employees with temporary, insecure first-day passwords creates significant security vulnerabilities. These credentials are often transmitted via unencrypted channels and frequently remain in use, increasing the risk of unauthorized access.

articles.title: Palo Alto Warns of Exploitation of VPN Bypass Exploits (CVE-2026-0257) in PAN-OS Flaw
articles.summary: Palo Alto Networks has confirmed that attackers are actively exploiting a critical authentication bypass vulnerability (CVE-2026-0257) affecting GlobalProtect VPN gateways, despite a patch being released on May 13.

articles.title: 152 Chrome Wallpaper Extensions with 105K Installs Linked to Adware and Fake Traffic
articles.summary: Researchers identified 152 malicious Chrome extensions masquerading as wallpaper add-ons that have infected over 105,000 users with adware and fake traffic generators. These extensions were distributed across 38 separate developer accounts to avoid detection.

articles.title: PhishLumos: Exposing phishing campaigns that evade detection by hiding content
articles.summary: PhishLumos is a research initiative designed to expose phishing campaigns that utilize cloaking techniques to bypass automated security detection systems. The tool addresses the growing sophistication of attackers who hide malicious content to evade interception.

articles.title: Modat enhances Magnify with Passive DNS for faster threat hunting and infrastructure analysis
articles.summary: Modat has integrated native Passive DNS intelligence into its Magnify platform, allowing security teams to consolidate IP, device, and certificate data into a single investigation workflow. This update aims to streamline threat hunting and infrastructure analysis by uncovering data often missed by conventional scanners.

articles.title: Microsoft’s workplace check-in via Wi-Fi tracks who’s in the office, and not everyone’s happy
articles.summary: Microsoft is introducing a Wi-Fi-based workplace check-in feature for Teams and Microsoft Places that automatically tracks employee office presence. While Microsoft claims the data is not stored as location history, the feature is controlled at the employer level, sparking privacy and surveillance concerns among labor advocates.

articles.title: LTM’s BlueVerse for iRun applies agentic AI to managed IT operations
articles.summary: LTM has launched BlueVerse for iRun, a managed services platform that leverages agentic AI to automate and optimize complex IT operations in hybrid cloud and SaaS environments. The solution aims to transition IT management from traditional, labor-intensive models to an outcome-driven, platform-led approach.

articles.title: Over 50 Android Apps Found Spreading MagicAd Trojan via Official Stores
articles.summary: Researchers discovered over 50 malicious Android applications on official stores that deploy the MagicAd trojan to display intrusive background advertisements. These apps utilize sophisticated system-level techniques to maintain ad activity even when the applications are not actively running.

articles.title: Popular WordPress Plugin Scripts Tampered to Plant Hidden Backdoors on Sites
articles.summary: Attackers injected malicious code into legitimate JavaScript files for popular WordPress plugins, allowing them to create unauthorized admin accounts and install backdoors when administrators logged in. This supply-chain attack specifically targeted sites using PushEngage, OptinMonster, and TrustPulse.

articles.title: Supply Chain Attack Hits Popular WordPress Plugins Through Awesome Motive CDN
articles.summary: Attackers compromised the Awesome Motive CDN to inject malicious JavaScript into popular WordPress plugins, impacting sites using OptinMonster, TrustPulse, and PushEngage. The attack enabled remote backdooring of affected websites without compromising the victims' servers directly.

articles.title: Infostealers, AI, and a 90% Affiliate Cut Fuel The Gentlemen group’s Rise
articles.summary: The Gentlemen ransomware gang has rapidly scaled their operations to target 483 victims globally by leveraging infostealer-acquired credentials, AI automation, and an aggressive 90% affiliate revenue-sharing model. The group has demonstrated significant activity, with the vast majority of these attacks occurring within the first half of 2026.

articles.title: Sniper Dz Scams Target MENA Users via Fake Facebook Offers and Browser Alerts
articles.summary: The threat actor Sniper Dz is targeting MENA users through fraudulent Facebook impersonation accounts that lure victims with fake subsidies and internet offers. These scams utilize deceptive social engineering tactics to compromise user information via browser alerts and malicious links.

articles.title: Palo Alto Warns of Active Exploitation of PAN-OS GlobalProtect VPN Flaw
articles.summary: Palo Alto Networks has confirmed that the CVE-2026-0257 authentication bypass vulnerability in its PAN-OS GlobalProtect software is being actively exploited by unknown attackers. This flaw allows unauthorized access to portals and gateways, posing a significant risk to affected organizations.

articles.title: Onspring CISO on where automated GRC systems fall short
articles.summary: Onspring CISO Nichole Windholz highlights the limitations of automated GRC systems, noting that simplified dashboards often overlook complex risks like insider behavior and vendor concentration. She emphasizes the need for deeper data validation to avoid the pitfalls of superficial risk monitoring.

articles.title: Proving what a military AI model will do is the real problem
articles.summary: Defense contractors are integrating frontier AI models into autonomous military systems, raising concerns about the difficulty of verifying and predicting model behavior in combat scenarios. This unpredictability poses a significant security challenge that existing arms control frameworks fail to address.

articles.title: Senior engineers are spending their week cleaning up AI-generated code
articles.summary: While AI tools are generating code that appears high-quality and bug-free during initial submission, senior engineers are reporting that this code frequently leads to increased production incidents and operational instability. This shift reflects a growing concern regarding the reliability of automated code generation in enterprise environments.

articles.title: Belarus-linked hackers target Gmail accounts of Polish public figures and their families
articles.summary: The Belarus-linked hacker group Ghostwriter is actively targeting the personal Gmail accounts of Polish public officials and their family members through expanded phishing operations. This development represents a concerning escalation in the group's efforts to compromise sensitive information held by high-profile political figures.

articles.title: Hackers Hide New Argamal Malware Inside Working Hentai Games
articles.summary: Researchers discovered the new Argamal malware embedded within functional hentai game installers distributed on adult websites and torrent platforms. The malware grants attackers remote access to compromised systems while masquerading as legitimate entertainment software.

articles.title: FBI disrupts massive AI-powered phishing service using a million URLs
articles.summary: The FBI, in collaboration with Google and Black Lotus Labs, successfully dismantled the 'Outsider Enterprise' phishing-as-a-service operation that utilized AI-driven tactics and thousands of malicious websites to steal user credentials and financial information.

articles.title: SECURITY AFFAIRS MALWARE NEWSLETTER ROUND 101
articles.summary: The Security Affairs Malware Newsletter, round 101, provides an overview of emerging threats including the IronWorm Rust-based malware, the Miasma npm worm, and a new variant of the Gafgyt botnet. It also covers techniques for leveraging AI agents to assist in malware analysis.

articles.title: Security Affairs newsletter Round 581 by Pierluigi Paganini – INTERNATIONAL EDITION
articles.summary: The latest edition of the Security Affairs newsletter covers curated industry news, including a report on the U.S. government halting the release of Anthropic's Fable 5 and Mythos 5 AI models.

articles.title: AI is code – and can't be prompted into being smarter
articles.summary: The article argues that AI models are fundamentally limited by their training data and code, dismissing the notion that they can be prompted to achieve a higher level of intelligence. It highlights that current AI systems are prone to blindly processing input, which can lead to unpredictable or undesirable outputs.

articles.title: Week in review: Exploited Check Point VPN zero-day, Oracle PeopleSoft servers under attack
articles.summary: This week's cybersecurity landscape highlighted active exploitation of a Check Point VPN zero-day and ongoing attacks against Oracle PeopleSoft servers. Additionally, a new open-source AI-powered tool called DockSec was introduced to enhance Docker container security.

articles.title: Ukrainian Extradited from Ireland Pleads Guilty Over Role in Conti Ransomware Scheme
articles.summary: Ukrainian national Oleksii Lytvynenko has pleaded guilty in a U.S. court to conspiracy charges related to his participation in the notorious Conti ransomware operation. He was extradited from Ireland to face charges for his role in global cyberattacks.

articles.title: Ex-school district employee jailed for hacks on former employer
articles.summary: A former Iowa school district IT employee was sentenced to 21 months in prison for carrying out a retaliatory cyberattack that disrupted classroom operations and caused significant financial damages. The attack involved unauthorized access to delete accounts and sabotage the district's systems.

articles.title: Anthropic disables new models after government calls them a national security concern
articles.summary: Anthropic has disabled its new Fable 5 and Mythos 5 models globally following a Commerce Department decree citing national security concerns. The move has triggered significant pushback from industry experts and researchers.

articles.title: Washington Pulled the Plug on Anthropic ‘s Fable 5 and Mythos 5 models. The Rest of the World Is Watching.
articles.summary: The U.S. Commerce Department has restricted the release of Anthropic’s Fable 5 and Mythos 5 AI models, prompting the company to challenge the decision due to a lack of transparency and technical evidence. The move has garnered significant international attention regarding AI regulatory oversight.

articles.title: Extradited Ukrainian Man Admits Role in Conti Ransomware Attacks
articles.summary: Ukrainian national Oleksii Lytvynenko has pleaded guilty in the US to his role in the Conti ransomware operation, which caused over $150 million in damages. The prosecution stems from a global campaign targeting more than 1,000 victims.

articles.title: Chinese hackers hijack auth flow, spy on isolated network for a decade
articles.summary: Chinese state-sponsored threat actors maintained unauthorized access to a victim's authentication infrastructure for ten years, allowing them to monitor administrative activities and persist within the target's isolated network. The breach highlights a significant, long-term intelligence-gathering operation focused on compromising secure identity management systems.

articles.title: Critical Splunk Enterprise Flaw Lets Attackers Run Code Without Authentication
articles.summary: Splunk has released patches for a critical 9.8 CVSS-rated vulnerability (CVE-2026-20253) that allows unauthenticated attackers to perform arbitrary file operations and remote code execution. Users are urged to update to versions 10.2.4 or 10.0.7 to remediate the flaw.

articles.title: US Gov asks Anthropic to ban 'foreign national' access to Fable, Mythos
articles.summary: The US government has ordered Anthropic to restrict foreign national access to its Fable 5 and Mythos 5 AI models, leading to a worldwide suspension of these tools. Anthropic is complying with the directive while contesting the government's justification for the restriction.

articles.title: U.S. CISA adds Oracle PeopleSoft Enterprise PeopleTools flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog
articles.summary: CISA has added the critical Oracle PeopleSoft Enterprise PeopleTools vulnerability, CVE-2026-35273, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog due to active exploitation. This vulnerability carries a CVSS score of 9.8, indicating a high risk of potential system compromise.

articles.title: U.S. Orders Anthropic to Suspend Fable 5 and Mythos 5 Access for Foreign Nationals
articles.summary: The U.S. government has ordered Anthropic to suspend access to its advanced AI models, Claude Fable 5 and Mythos 5, for foreign nationals due to national security concerns. Consequently, Anthropic will disable access to these models for all users.

articles.title: NanoClaw now armed with JFrog for safer packages
articles.summary: NanoClaw has integrated JFrog to improve the security of its software packages, highlighting a broader industry focus on securing AI agent development. The update emphasizes the risks associated with granting autonomous AI agents excessive system privileges.

articles.title: Tracing Digital Intent: New MacOS Tahoe 26 Artifact Discovered
articles.summary: Unit 42 researchers have identified a new macOS artifact called Tahoe 26 that logs user menu selections, providing new capabilities for digital forensics. This discovery enables investigators to better trace user activity across the operating system.

articles.title: FBI takes down massive China-based cybercrime network that caused $1.9B in losses
articles.summary: The FBI dismantled a China-based cybercrime network responsible for $1.9 billion in financial losses through a phishing infrastructure that impersonated delivery and government services. The operation targeted victims with deceptive lures regarding unpaid tolls, parking violations, and missed packages.

articles.title: Iran-Linked Handala Breached a California Water Utility. It Could Have Done Worse, and It Knows That.
articles.summary: The Iran-linked threat group Handala breached California Water Service through an exposed GPS tool, resulting in the unauthorized access and leakage of billing data for 2 million customers. The attackers published 5GB of stolen data as proof of the compromise.

articles.title: Maine disables data breach notification portal after fake disclosures
articles.summary: The state of Maine took its public data breach portal offline following the submission of fraudulent breach reports. The state is currently reviewing its authentication and submission procedures to prevent further abuse of the system.

articles.title: Over 400 Arch Linux AUR Packages Hijacked to Deploy Infostealer and eBPF Rootkit
articles.summary: Over 400 Arch Linux AUR packages were compromised by attackers who injected build scripts to deploy a credential-stealing Rust binary and an eBPF rootkit. This supply chain attack specifically targets developers building software from the community repository.

articles.title: 400+ Arch Linux AUR Packages Hijacked to Install Rust Credential Stealer
articles.summary: Attackers compromised over 400 Arch Linux AUR packages by injecting malicious build scripts that install a Rust-based credential stealer and an optional eBPF rootkit. This supply chain attack targets developers by executing the malware during the software build process.

articles.title: Google Sues Chinese Smishing Network Accused of Using Gemini AI in Phishing
articles.summary: Google has initiated legal action against a Chinese cybercrime network that allegedly leveraged its Gemini AI to develop and facilitate a phishing-as-a-service platform called Outsider. The operation targeted U.S. citizens through automated SMS-based phishing attacks.

articles.title: U.S. CISA adds Ivanti Sentry flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog and urges patching by June 14
articles.summary: CISA has added a critical vulnerability (CVE-2026-10520) in Ivanti Sentry to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog, requiring federal agencies to apply patches by June 14. The flaw carries a maximum CVSS score of 10.0 and is actively being exploited in the wild.

articles.title: Fired IT worker jailed for 21 months after sabotaging old school district
articles.summary: A former IT employee in Iowa was sentenced to 21 months in prison for sabotaging his previous school district's computer systems. The perpetrator was caught after confiding in a former colleague about his malicious activities.

articles.title: US, France, and Italian authorities shut down massive deepfake porn site
articles.summary: Authorities from the US, France, and Italy collaborated to dismantle a prominent website that distributed non-consensual deepfake pornography targeting high-profile individuals. The operation marks a significant international effort to combat the weaponization of synthetic media for harassment.

articles.title: phpBB forum fixes auth bypass bug lurking for a decade
articles.summary: The phpBB forum software has patched a decade-old authentication bypass vulnerability that permitted unauthorized access to user and administrator accounts. The flaw was identified and addressed, effectively eliminating a long-standing security risk for forum administrators.

articles.title: China-Linked Hackers Backdoored Linux Login Software to Hide for Nearly a Decade
articles.summary: A China-linked threat actor known as Velvet Ant compromised Linux PAM and OpenSSH components to maintain persistent, long-term backdoor access for nearly a decade. By targeting core authentication systems, the group successfully avoided detection during standard security cleanups.

articles.title: Atomic Arch Campaign Hijacks 20+ Linux AUR Packages to Deliver Malware
articles.summary: The 'Atomic Arch' campaign compromised over 20 Linux AUR packages by exploiting ownership transfers to distribute rootkit-like malware to users. This supply chain attack poses a significant threat to Arch Linux users by facilitating unauthorized access through tainted software packages.

articles.title: Ukrainian national pleads guilty to role in Conti ransomware operation
articles.summary: A Ukrainian national extradited to the U.S. has pleaded guilty to conspiracy charges related to their involvement in the Conti ransomware group. This development marks a significant legal action against a member of one of the most prominent cybercriminal syndicates.

articles.title: Conti ransomware group member pleads guilty, faces up to 20 years in prison
articles.summary: Oleksii Lytvynenko, a member of the Conti ransomware group, has pleaded guilty to cybercrime charges and faces a maximum sentence of 20 years in prison. The conviction follows his arrest in Ireland in 2023 for activities conducted between 2021 and his detention.

articles.title: Bankruptcy admin approves settlement fund of $47 million for 23andMe data breach victims
articles.summary: A bankruptcy administrator has approved a $47 million settlement fund to compensate approximately 7 million 23andMe customers impacted by a 2023 data breach. The incident involved the theft and exposure of sensitive genetic and personal information on the dark web.

articles.title: Major US surveillance program poised to lapse after legislative deadlock
articles.summary: The US surveillance program authorized under Section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act has lapsed for the first time due to a legislative deadlock in Congress. This expiration interrupts the government's ability to conduct warrantless electronic surveillance on foreign targets.
